topic: DeepSeek Harness Agent Workflow Plugin: Orchestrate Multi-Step Agent Runs

key_points: Standalone DeepSeek Harness Web UI plugin (126 stars, 23 forks, MIT, TypeScript, created 2026-08-18) that adds a 'Workflow' tab alongside the built-in 'Conversation' and 'Trajectory' tabs
Uses user conversation turns as the entry point, rendering model requests, model responses, and tool calls as a clear execution chain
Does NOT replace or modify DSH's built-in 'Trajectory' feature

Key features: browse by turn (left panel lists user turns with prompt summary, start time, model-call count, tool-call count, completion status); execution-chain visualization (request/response/tool-call cards per model call); full request inspection (real system prompt, provider-agnostic messages[], tools as collapsible JSON trees); response inspection (reasoning, content, tool calls, raw record); tool execution status (running/done/failed with args, result, duration, error summary); token & cache stats (input, uncached input, cache-read, cache-write, output); virtualized rendering for long chains
Data source: real events recorded in the DSH Session — never inferred or re-assembled from Harness source; plugin only reads/displays, never injects messages/prompts/tools
Compatibility: v0.1.x only targets dsh@0.1.0-rc.8; DSH is pre-release so RC client interfaces may change — must reinstall matching plugin version after DSH upgrade

Install: npx --yes @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.0-rc.8 plugin --profile web add ./dsh-plugin-agent-workflow-0.1.1.tgz --workspace-root; or from GitHub pinned tag github:xuanyuanzhifeng/dsh-plugin-agent-workflow#v0.1.1
Known limits: summary only covers client-loadable session history; no shareable deep links; multiple tool calls in one response shown as linear scrollable sequence (no parallel branch graph)

Official-bundle-form, zero-core-patch DSH plugin (110 stars, 4 forks, MIT, TypeScript, created 2026-08-12) that brings Claude Code's UltraCode mode to DSH — upgrades DSH's one-shot multi-agent dispatch into a workflow layer that is generatable, saveable, governable, observable, and recoverable

Does NOT replace DSH's built-in foreground 'workflow' tool; that native tool is for 'run several things in parallel this once' — this plugin adds higher-level process-product capabilities: naming, discovery, generation, reuse, pause/resume, rerun/continue, durable evidence, cost records, governance

Value table: one-shot dispatch (re-prompt decomposition each round, parallel results scattered in session, restart from scratch on interrupt, constraints via prompt) vs DSH Workflow (save as named project/personal workflow, durable run graph/events/artifacts/results/cost, rerun from run snapshot or continue via effect cache, manifest+preflight+runtime hard limits, capability-only VM + JSON boundaries + deterministic guards + approval tiers)

Quick start: dsh plugin --profile web add "github:dsh-external/dsh_workflow#main"; commands /workflow list, /workflow parallel-investigation {...}, /workflow create ..., /workflow review --risk high ..., /workflow runs

Model-callable tools: workflow_list (discover built-in/pattern/project/personal workflows), run_workflow (run named workflow, scout-then-author from natural language, or run restricted inline workflow), workflow_manage (view/pause/resume/stop/rerun/continue/save/rename/revise/delete/cleanup)

KodaX-parity execution model: versioned dsh.workflow v1 capsule (manifest, source, intent, inputs, requires, provenance); unified async function run(wf, args); full WorkflowApi (phase, spawnAgent, runAgent, wait, snapshot/output, send/stop, parallel, pipeline, synthesize, single-level nested workflow, artifact, log, budget); runAgent returns null on ordinary subtask failure for policy-based degradation

Two built-ins: parallel-investigation (rubric/agent/concurrency parameterized) and scoped-review (packet/schema/read-contract/dual-primary/per-finding verifier/audit artifact); six standard patterns: classify-and-act, fan-out-and-synthesize, adversarial-verification, generate-and-filter, tournament, loop-until-done

Deterministic discovery order: plugin built-ins → project .dsh/workflows → personal $DSH_HOME/workflows; project overrides personal; .workflow.json beats .ts/.mjs/.js in same dir; symlinks, path escape, oversized files, unknown capsule fields, version incompat, manifest/filename mismatch all fail before execution
179 passing tests; DSH 0.0.1-rc.2 snapshot; Node >=22.19

Persistent, reusable multi-model Agent teams for DeepSeek Harness (159 stars, 2 forks, MIT, TypeScript, created 2026-08-15) — give each member its own model, role, fallback route, token limit, and tool policy
A team is a reusable product object, not a one-off dispatch form: create once in Settings → Teams, use across projects and conversations

Capabilities: one model/tool policy per member; dynamic workflow planning by default (active conversation's model assigns focused work and dependencies); Team/Solo/Inherited modes; bounded DAG with retries, quality gate, background work (observable, cancellable, finite, restart-safe); official provider token usage (input/cache-read/cache-write/output, never invented prices); versions, recipes, definition backup

Install: dsh plugin --profile web add -w github:toolclub/dsh-agent-team-gui#v1.0.1; requires DSH >=0.1.0-rc.5 <0.2.0, Web profile, Node >=22.19.0 <23 or >=24.0.0 (Node 23 unsupported), pnpm; may need allowBuilds in ~/.dsh/profiles/web/pnpm-workspace.yaml

First team in five steps: create reusable members (provider/model, role prompt, fallback route, tool grants) → create team and select members (Fixed order off for dynamic planning, on for serial pipeline) → choose Always/Smart/Manual activation, all/adaptive subset, foreground/background, resilience/budget/review controls → choose Team/Solo/Inherited beside composer → run
Official DeepSeek Harness repo (203,079 stars, 23,410 forks, MIT, TypeScript, created 2026-08-13) — 'Everything is a Plugin'

Built-in model-facing workflow tool @deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-workflow: call it with a JavaScript orchestration script, an identity block (meta), and optional args; it runs the script over ctx.workflowEngine, fanning work out across subagents until the script's final value returns

Use the workflow tool only when the user explicitly asks for workflow-style or large multi-agent orchestration (audit over many files, migration, multi-angle research); prefer plain subagent calls for one or two delegations
Call params: meta (required: name, description; optional whenToUse, phases), script (required plain JS body, no export const meta), args (optional JSON object exposed as the args global)
Success returns canonical envelope { runId, agentsStarted, result }; non-clean finish is an error, never partial output; cancellation bridged from parent step's abort signal
Config: toolName (default 'workflow'), maxResultChars (default 50000)
Engine: dsh-workflow-worker-thread — node:worker_threads, one worker per run, script's vm context inside; one engine per context provides ctx.workflowEngine (no named-provider registry)
WorkflowStartRequest: script, meta, args, optional subagentProvider, optional maxTotalAgents (per-run total-child ceiling), parent (REQUIRED — every child attributed to it), signal
WorkflowMeta field vocabulary matches Claude Code dynamic-workflows meta block; phases is progress vocabulary only (phase() calls match titles for observers, no execution structure implied)
WorkflowResult: value (script's materialized return value, plain host JSON), stopReason (CLOSED union: completed | cancelled | error), error (present iff not completed)

Durable session records: four log-only events (run-start, member starts/endings filtered by run.id, run-end) projected into the calling Agent's Session; nested transport calls execute normally but write no record

Adaptive deep-research orchestrator plugin for DeepSeek Harness (20 stars, 3 forks, MIT, TypeScript, created 2026-08-06) built on the official DSH workflow engine (ctx.workflows / @deepseek-ai/dsh-workflow-workerthread)
Designed with cybernetics + information theory, not a fixed-prompt pipeline — a living, adaptive research closed loop

Mechanisms: planning agent defines answer space (scope) + acceptance criteria per sub-question; enumerates information dimensions (Ashby's law of requisite variety) with coverage_gaps self-check; research subagents maintain three-state evidence (confirmed/uncertain/gaps); marginal-information-gain (EIG) verification — stop after one consecutive zero-gain round + hard round cap; closed-loop replanning (round 1 parallel research on all sub-questions, auto-dispatch follow-up rounds on high-priority gaps until marginal gain ≈ 0); rate-distortion lossy compression into final report; optional adversarial review subagent (citation spot-check, coverage audit, overconfidence flagging)

Install: dsh plugin --profile <profile> add git+https://github.com/dsh-external/dsh-deep-research.git; tool deep_research injected per profile; model auto-triggers on deep-research/research/report requests

angles: The plugin ecosystem is the differentiator: DSH's 'Everything is a Plugin' architecture means multi-step orchestration is a swappable capability — the built-in workflow tool, the Web UI workflow tab, the UltraCode-style workflow layer, and persistent agent teams are all separate plugins you can mix and match

Built-in workflow tool vs plugin workflow layer: the native tool is for one-shot parallel fan-out; plugins (dsh_workflow) add durable, named, governable, resumable workflow products — know when each applies

The 'agent as a unit of programming' model: model-written JS orchestration scripts (parallel, pipeline, loops) that fan out subagents and return a single JSON value — fewer round-trips, less token waste than step-by-step tool calls

Traceability and observability as the core value: the workflow tab renders real session events (system prompt, messages[], tools, token/cache stats) so you can debug multi-step runs; durable run graphs and effect caches make long workflows restart-safe
Safety and governance: capability-only VM, JSON boundaries, deterministic guards, approval tiers, per-run maxTotalAgents ceilings, and preflight validation before any real subagent starts

Cost/performance trade-offs: parallel subagents and dynamic workflows consume significantly more tokens — reserve for heavy tasks (audits, migrations, multi-angle research), prefer plain subagent calls for one or two delegations

Compatibility gotchas: DSH is pre-release (RC versions), so plugin versions must match the DSH snapshot; Node version constraints (>=22.19, Node 23 unsupported); allowBuilds permission for Git dependencies

Comparison: built-in workflow tool vs dsh-plugin-agent-workflow (Web UI) vs dsh_workflow (UltraCode layer) vs dsh-agent-team-gui (persistent teams) vs dsh-deep-research (adaptive research) — where each fits in the 2026 DSH orchestration landscape
